patch_description:
Replace the single-sample reversal decision with a residual-noise-calibrated alpha-beta tracker and a two-sample directional confirmation gate. The current MAD estimate measures the full window amplitude, which confuses genuine oscillation magnitude with measurement noise. Estimating robust residual noise after the local linear fit provides a more appropriate uncertainty scale for tracker gains and reversal thresholds.

A reversal is accepted immediately for a sufficiently strong, slope-supported movement, preserving responsiveness at genuine turning points. Weak opposite movements must persist for two samples before changing direction, substantially reducing noise-driven slope changes and false reversals. Innovation clipping additionally prevents isolated observations from causing large tracker excursions. This retains causal newest-sample alignment and O(N·W) vectorized fitting plus O(N) tracking latency.
